newsitem.title: USA: Stolt-Nielsen Q3 hurt by inventory slump.
newsitem.headline: Stolt-Nielsen Q3 hurt by inventory slump.

text.p: Stolt-Nielsen SA said on Thursday a decline in shipping inventories hurt results at its Stolt Parcel Tankers Inc division and third quarter results.
This division had a record performance in the third quarter 1995, when trade volumes and freight rates were boosted by inventory buildup, particularly in Asia.
The company also said during the recent quarter, spot rates fell during after modest increases in the second quarter. But spot rates seem to have stabilized, Stolt said.

"The performance of our tanker business during the quarter was adversely affected by pricing uncertainty in the markets for hydrocarbons and reduced demand due to inventory drawdown," President and Chief Operating Officer Christopher Wright said. Stolt-Nielsen provides transportation services for bulk liquid chemicals, edible oils, acids and other specialty liquids.
Stolt said its fleet continued to have a high utilization rate in the quarter although at lower freight rates for spot commodities.

But Stolt said the underlying worldwide economic environment had improved and it expected the unfavorable short-term inventory cycle to reverse in the coming months, helping both cargo volumes and freight rates.
Wright said he remained optimistic about prospects for the company's transportation business.

The company said its Stolt Tank Containers unit had a strong performance in the quarter despite increased price pressures in recent quarters. Shipments rose 12 percent in the first three quarters this year compared to the same period last year.
